scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Dhunuchi Nritya is a Bengali Hindu traditional dance performed during puja and aarti ceremonies.
It celebrates the victory of Goddess Durga over Mahishasura.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed during the last days of Durga Puja, specifically between Ashtami and Dashami, to celebrate victory and empowerment.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Dhunuchi dance at Samajsevi Sangh V 20181017 112000.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c9/Dhunuchi_dance_at_Samajsevi_Sangh_V_20181017_112000.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance involves holding one or two dhunuchis, while experts may hold three (two in hands, one in mouth).
It is performed to the rhythm of the dhak, kansor, and ghanta.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Communal, aiming to involve the community as a whole.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is purely instrumental, featuring the dhak, kansor, and ghanta.
These instruments produce loud, heavy sounds.
Listen for the Dhak, Kansor, Ghanta.
The sound is dominated by the loud, heavy, and rhythmic beat of the dhak drum, accompanied by the metallic resonance of the kansor and ghanta.
